newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan to lease tourism resort to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to lease tourism resort to foreigners.

text.p: Jordan is inviting foreign investors to submit offers for the long-term lease of a hot spring resort owned by financially troubled Jordan Tourism and Spa Company, an investment official said on Saturday.

Jordan Investment Corporation (JIC), the investment arm of the government, which owns 70 percent of the company, says it is seeking offers from interested foreign parties for a 20-25 year lease at a negotiable $2 million rent annually.

Munzir al-Saudi, deputy head of JIC, said the corporation is also open to discuss future ownership of the company premises, which include a hotel and chalet complex in Jordan's prime hot water springs of Maeen near the Dead Sea, the lowest point on earth.

The Jordan Tourism and Spa Company which posted half a million dinars in operating profits in 1995 alone, was delisted from the Amman Financial Market after total accumulative losses exceeded its five million dinar ($7.0 million capital).
Losses now stand at 9.68 million dinars.
The foreign company which would manage and run the resort would not be responsible for any losses already incurred, Saudi said.
Past losses were primarily due to bad management and a 2.9 million dinar furniture contract made in 1989 that is now under investigation, officials said.
The government, which ruled out liquidating the company despite the losses, is keen to salvage the company by offering its assets for lease.
